subject: Post-demo: capacity fit & next validation steps for Dedicated vs Hyperscaler
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo: capacity fit & next validation steps for Dedicated vs Hyperscaler

Hi Amy —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and a proposed short validation plan so we can compare Dedicated Redwood capacity vs the hyperscaler reserved/committed options you mentioned (GCP committed use + AWS Savings Plans).

Key notes from the demo:
- Primary workload: low-latency chat + episodic batch embedding jobs (peak concurrency ~2200 concurrent chat sessions during business hours; nightly batch of ~50M tokens).
- p99 latency target for chat: <= 220ms at 8k context (95% availability).
- Cost objective: reduce per-100k-token inference cost vs current managed endpoint by >= 25% while keeping p99 SLA.
- Data: customer PII occasionally included, must remain in-region (US-east).
- Procurement: you have a 2026 budget window and CU commitments on GCP that run through Q1 2027.

What we propose as the minimal test matrix (please confirm):
1) Sustained throughput soak (72 hrs): provision a small Dedicated pool sized to sustain your peak concurrency profile and run steady-state traffic to measure p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, and cost per token.
2) Autoscale & burst behavior: simulate burst traffic to validate Redwood Dedicated autoscaling latency vs hyperscaler cold-start + preemption behavior.
3) Failure & fallback: controlled failover where we route traffic to a lower-cost variant (quantized) and compare quality regressions and latency delta.
4) Cost compare: side-by-side normalized cost per 1M tokens including overhead (network, egress, reserved amortization).

What we need from Nimbus to start (if you approve the plan):
- A short sample of production traffic characteristics (synth load is fine): typical prompt lengths, average tokens per chat, expected concurrency curve by hour.
- Procurement lead and expected timeline for a trial Dedicated pool (this helps us align capacity reservation windows).
- NDA/MOU if you prefer before exchanging specifics.

I've attached a one-page evaluation checklist and a draft test-config we can use to provision the Dedicated trial. If the plan looks good I'll follow up with a concrete test schedule and provisional cost estimate for the trial.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications / constraints from our side before we commit to the 72-hr soak:

- Procurement timeline: we have approvals queued but our procurement requires a pricing band and SOW before hardware-level provisioning. Ideally we want a 30-day trial window that doesn't require a long-term commitment up front.
- Committed discounts: we currently have substantial CU discounts with GCP through Q1 2027; finance will want a modeled comparison vs that effective hourly price (including our CU amortized).
- Residency: US-east with logs retained for 90 days. We will only provide synthetic traffic to avoid sharing PII during the trial.
- SLA ask: can you provide a target SLA for p99 and an outline of how Redwood handles capacity preemption/fallback? We care most about graceful degradation (not erroring out) and predictable latency increase under load.

Also, please share a sample of the test harness you plan to run (ramp profile, traffic generator). We can run an initial smoke test on our end before provisioning anything.

Amy

Director of Platform Engineering, Nimbus AI

Hi Amy — thanks for the quick reply and the constraints. Below is a slightly more prescriptive test matrix and the exact metrics we'll capture so finance/procurement can map apples-to-apples with your GCP commitments.

Proposed test plan (short-form):
- Duration: 72-hour soak (48h steady-state + 24h ramp/burst + failover window).
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool provisioned in us-east1, GPU type: A100 80GB (config TBD with your procurement). We can also run a parallel test on a hyperscaler instance type you specify for comparison (we'll supply an AWS/GCP cost-normalization sheet).

Metrics to capture (per-run):
- p50/p95/p99 latency at 1k/4k/8k contexts
- tokens/sec and inferred cost per 1M tokens (normalized)
- GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV cache hit rate
- Autoscale reaction time (ms) when adding nodes under load
- Preemption rate / instance interruptions (for hyperscaler runs)
- Error rate (5xx) and graceful-fallback count (times we routed to quantized variant)

Pass/fail thresholds (example):
- p99 <= 220ms for chat at 8k context during steady-state
- error rate < 0.5%
- cost per 1M tokens <= your current managed endpoint cost * 0.75 (i.e., 25% reduction)

Attachments: I've uploaded the redwood-eval-matrix.xlsx (matrix + normalization sheet) and the ramp-script.sh we use for the soak. We will provide a short smoke harness you can run locally before we provision anything.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You share the synthetic profile (or let us build one from your high-level numbers).
2) We schedule a 30-minute alignment session with Sales Engineering + Procurement (I can include Marissa for pricing and Sean for dev-ops details).
3) We provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the 72-hour run and invite your team to observe metrics in the Redwood Console.

If that sounds good I can draft a short SOW that keeps the trial non-binding but commits to the provisioning windows so we don't oversubscribe capacity.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
